dimensions.assessment: Affects satellite operators, telecommunications companies applying for licenses, and federal regulatory agencies.
dimensions.evidence: applications for a license or grant of market access to operate a system described in subsection (c)(1)(B)

dimensions.assessment: Imposes strict 1-year deadlines on the FCC for license determinations and establishes legal preemption of state and local rate regulations.
dimensions.evidence: a State or local government may not regulate the rates charged by an applicant or licensee

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal spending amounts are mentioned, though application fees under section 8 are referenced.
dimensions.evidence: the applicant has paid the fee, if any, required under section 8

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to add comprehensive radiofrequency licensing authorities and national security review procedures.
dimensions.evidence: Part I of title III of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 301 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Sets initial license and market access terms up to 15 years with permanent statutory framework changes.
dimensions.evidence: The Commission shall grant a license for a term not to exceed 15 years

importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates statutory deadlines and procedures for FCC licensing and market access decisions regarding satellite and telecommunications operations.
